data.name: Shukriyyah
data.long_meaning: A person who is thankful and shows gratitude. One who is blessed and acknowledges Allah's blessings.
data.spiritual_meaning: Cultivating a heart of gratitude and recognizing the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us.

in_arabic.name: شكرية
in_arabic.long_meaning: شكرية هي اسم علم مؤنث مشتق من الفعل شكر الذي يعني حمد الله على نعمته، ويتضمن مفهوم الامتنان والشكر لله على كل ما يحييه، وقد ذکر الشكر في القرآن الكريم في العديد من الآيات

in_urdu.name: شکریہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: شکریہ ایک عربی نام ہے جو شکر کرنے والی کی意思 رکھتا ہے، اور اس کا استعمال اسلامی روایت میں بہت زیادہ ہے، اس نام کا ذکر قرآن پاک میں بھی ہے

in_hindi.name: शुक्रिया
in_hindi.long_meaning: शुक्रिया एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है शुक्र और कृतज्ञता की भावना, और इसका उपयोग इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत अधिक है, इस नाम का उल्लेख कुरान में भी है

in_pashto.name: شکریه
in_pashto.long_meaning: شکریه د عربي نوم دی چې مانا یې د مننې او شکر کولو ښودنه ده، او ددې نوم کارونه په اسلامي روایت کې ډېر دی، دغه نوم په قرآن کریم کې هم ذکر شوی دی

in_english.name: Shukriyyah
in_english.long_meaning: Shukriyyah is an Arabic name derived from the root shukr, meaning gratitude and appreciation to God, and is mentioned in the Quran, it signifies a personality trait of being thankful and appreciative

data.cultural_impact: The name Shukriyyah holds a significant cultural impact within the Islamic community, as it represents a value that is highly regarded in Islamic teachings - gratitude. Gratitude towards Allah (SWT) is an essential aspect of Islamic faith, and the name Shukriyyah serves as a constant reminder of this. It is also a nod to the importance of expressing gratitude to others in daily life, which is a integral part of being a good member of society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shukriyyah holds deep significance, as it reflects a person's attitude towards Allah and the world around them. A person named Shukriyyah is understood to be someone who acknowledges the blessings they have been given and seeks to live a life of gratitude. This spiritual mindset is deeply rooted in Islamic teachings, which emphasize the importance of recognizing and expressing gratitude to Allah for the countless blessings He bestows upon us. Ultimately, the name Shukriyyah reminds us of the importance of living a life of gratitude and using our blessings to serve and benefit others, both in our personal relationships and in the larger community.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Al-Athir's 'Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh' (1260 CE) The name Shukriyyah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shukriyyah bint Taj al-Din Abd al-Mu'min, a daughter of the Seljuk Sultan Taj al-Din Abd al-Mu'min (r. 1105-1118 CE), was known for her piety and generosity towards scholars and dervishes. Her name Shukriyyah means 'grateful' in Arabic, reflecting her character.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar' (1377 CE) The name Shukriyyah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shukriyyah bint al-Hasan al-Marwazi, a wealthy woman from Marw (present-day Mary, Afghanistan), is mentioned by Ibn Khaldun for her patronage of scholars, particularly theologians and Sufis, during the Mongol invasion of the region in the late 13th century CE. Her name Shukriyyah means 'grateful' or 'thankful' in Arabic.
